title: Native evidence closed schemas v2 (PROPOSED design reference)
description: Closed Draft 2020-12 records for the native evidence contract. Exact typed admission (foundation/canonical.py) precedes validation: integers are exact JSON integer literals, booleans are not integers, no float/exponent/-0, no duplicate keys, no lone surrogates. The import2 wrapper itself is foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/import; these are its native typed payloads plus native context/coverage/protocol records. Revision after Codex review v2: per-language co-located units (WorkspaceUnitV2/UnitMembershipV1), inert generated-file rows with a read-only virtual OUT_DIR, workflow canonical import payloads with native adapter-input shapes, ImportRegistryRowV1, preparedResolution, principal join, StageAuthorityV1. Blind-consumer corrections: the closed TypeScript native context (TypeScriptNativeContextV2 and family, domain native.context.typescript.v2, carrying typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot) and the subject-scope commitment / coverage-admission records.

x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.standing: Normative and CLOSED. For every DeficiencyV2 member, WHICH retained field carries its cause and what that field must say. There is no default row: a deficiency with no row here is a registry defect and refuses. Nothing in this registry changes DeficiencyV2, NativeCause, UnresolvedEdgeKindV1, ClosedWorldV2, the public DomainDetailCode registry or any D9 class, code or exit; every carrier it names already exists and is already closed.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.whyItIsNeeded: native-evidence section 10 labels its second column `Cause (nativeCause)` and then fills three of its rows with values that are not NativeCause members: `the unresolved edge classes; partial/not-attempted stage` for `resolution-incomplete`, `exports-open, exports-unknown` for `external-consumers-unknown`, and `compiler-inferred present` for `derivation-policy-unmet`. Each refuses schema validation as a nativeCause (`'computed-member-access' is not valid under any of the given schemas`), so the only representable value was null - which the NativeCause description itself defines as `a disclosure was owed and not made`. Worse, nothing compared the pair to anything: on the frozen reference a `resolution-incomplete` entry carrying the unrelated but schema-valid `lockfile-missing`, or relabelled `capability-missing`, or a `derivation-policy-unmet` with an empty derivationKinds, or an `external-consumers-unknown` over `exportsClosed: closed`, each closed a Run. A cause vocabulary that nothing derives and nothing compares leaves the disclosure optional in practice - the same argument that added the three body-language-* members, carried through to the rest of the table.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.whyNotMoreEnumMembers: Adding NativeCause members was rejected on the merits, not for compatibility. `resolution-incomplete` has a genuinely SET-VALUED cause: an entry can exhibit up to all sixteen UnresolvedEdgeKindV1 classes at once, and a scalar cannot carry them, so enum members would either lose information or force an arbitrary pick - the multi-cause defect the finding names. All three rows already have closed, structured, independently DERIVED carriers in the same record: unresolvedEdgeClasses (which RC-2 already forces to equal the admitted unresolved-edge facts), ClosedWorldV2.exportsClosed, and derivationKinds. The correction is to NAME those carriers and ENFORCE the join, not to duplicate them in a scalar.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.nullIsNotAnEscape: Where a row says nativeCause MUST be null, that null no longer records an unmade disclosure: the row names the field that carries the cause instead, and admission REFUSES unless that field actually carries it. A `resolution-incomplete` entry whose resolutionCompleteness claims `complete` is refused, so `null` cannot be used to say nothing.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.multiCauseAndPrecedence: An entry carries ONE deficiency and simultaneously carries every carrier this registry names. What each carrier RETAINS differs, and an earlier revision wrongly generalised the strongest case to all of them by saying the scalar `loses nothing`. The accurate statement is per carrier: resolutionCompleteness.unresolvedEdgeClasses is a genuine SET and retains EVERY applicable unresolved class at once, already forced by RC-2 to equal the admitted unresolved-edge facts of the view; closedWorld and derivationKinds are independent fields that retain their own state whatever the deficiency is; but input-closure-incomplete's carrier is a SINGLE SCALAR NativeCause, and a Run can genuinely be missing several inputs at once - two absent crates, or an absent crate AND an unavailable generated file. For that row the retained cause is a SELECTED one, not the full set. See selectedScalarCauseLimitation. Which single deficiency is declared when several apply is the section 10 precedence order, applied by the owning sufficiency evaluation against a REQUIREMENT. That selection is deliberately NOT re-derived from the entry alone, and the limit is stated rather than worked around: several conditions are requirement-relative (external-consumer state matters only for a universal negative about an exported target; the confidence floor lives in the Requirement, not the entry), and RC-3 makes `coverage: complete` with `state: incomplete` and NO deficiency a valid honest entry. Forcing a deficiency from exhibited entry evidence would therefore refuse lawful Runs. What IS decidable from the entry is the direction enforced here: a DECLARED deficiency must be SUPPORTED by the entry's own committed evidence.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.retainedVersusPublicRoute: Two different routes and neither substitutes for the other. RETAINED: the whole ViewEntryV3 lives inside the coverage2 record, whose payload digest and schema digest the Run commits, so every carrier named below is retained evidence a verifier can re-derive. PUBLIC: the DEFICIENCY is projected outward as its own closed DomainDetailCode - `resolution-incomplete`, `external-consumers-unknown` and `derivation-policy-unmet` are all already members - and the CAUSE travels as typed detail in the coverage2 record the host termination names by its coverageId, exactly as section 10 has always said for the nativeCause-carried rows. No new public code is added and none is needed.

language-tier-unsupported.rule: The admitted universe's selected grammars do not bear the requested relation@rung. The cause is a single named state, so nativeCause carries it and must be exactly capability-missing. Already derived and enforced by the syntax capability prerequisite; stated here so one table covers every member.

provider-unavailable.rule: Section 10 leaves this row's Cause cell empty, so a null is lawful and self-describing; where a more specific named state applies it is carried. No other cause may appear.

input-closure-incomplete.rule: The one deficiency whose cause genuinely IS a single named missing input, which is why section 10 lists twelve of them and why the three body-language-* members were added here. A null refuses: this row is exactly where a null would record an unmade disclosure.

budget-exhausted.rule: Section 10 already qualifies this row `(stage terminal)`. The stage terminal is the cause and it is a closed StageTerminal value in the same entry, so nativeCause is null by design and the terminal must actually say budget-exhausted.

confidence-floor-unmet.rule: Requirement-relative and deliberately without an entry carrier: the FLOOR lives in RequirementV2.minConfidenceMillionths and the entry carries only its own confidenceMillionths, so the entry cannot decide whether the floor was met. The comparison is the sufficiency evaluation's, and stating that limit is honest where inventing an entry-level predicate would not be.

derivation-policy-unmet.relationLaw: The OWNING law scopes this deficiency to one relation. Native section 4.7 and sufficiency_v2 apply derivationPolicy only where `rel == "types"` and the requirement asks for `declared-only`; there is no derivation policy for any other relation, so no other relation's entry can be short of one. An earlier revision checked the derivationKinds carrier ALONE, and a complete Run therefore admitted this declared deficiency on a `references` entry that merely carried the same array value (root diagnostic: references ADMIT, types ADMIT). An entry whose relation is outside this list cannot declare it.
derivation-policy-unmet.rule: Section 10's Cause cell reads `compiler-inferred present`, which is a statement about derivationKinds - a closed three-member set in this same entry - and not a NativeCause. The entry must actually carry compiler-inferred among its derivation kinds.
derivation-policy-unmet.thisIsDeclarationSupportNotAnObligation: Two different assertions, and only the first is enforced. (1) An entry that DECLARES this deficiency must be for relation `types` and must actually carry `compiler-inferred`. (2) Whether a given requirement DEMANDS the deficiency is sufficiency_v2's question against a RequirementV2, and is not derived here. `compiler-inferred` types are exact under the admitted universe and are perfectly valid under `derivationPolicy=any`; they become a deficiency only under `declared-only`. Nothing here imposes declared-only on a valid types entry, and controls hold both directions.

resolution-incomplete.rule: Section 10's Cause cell reads `the unresolved edge classes; partial/not-attempted stage`, and both halves are ResolutionCompletenessV2 fields: `state` names the stage condition and `unresolvedEdgeClasses` carries EVERY applicable class at once, already forced by RC-2 to equal the admitted unresolved-edge facts of this view. A claim of this deficiency over a `complete` or `not-applicable` resolution state is refused: that is the entry contradicting its own evidence.

external-consumers-unknown.rule: Section 10's Cause cell reads `exports-open, exports-unknown`, which are the ClosedWorldV2 exportsClosed values `open` and `unknown` in this same entry, not NativeCause members. `closed` refuses: an entry cannot claim its consumers are unknown while its own closed-world record says they are closed.

required-relation-missing.rule: A sufficiency verdict about a relation the view does NOT carry an entry for, so an entry can never be its own evidence. It has no entry carrier by construction and takes no cause. Kept admissible rather than refused because nothing in this contract states that a host may not record it, and inventing that refusal is not this correction's to make.

x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.noDeficiencyNoCause: A null deficiency requires a null nativeCause. A cause without a deficiency names why nothing went wrong, which is not a claim this record can carry.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.enforcedAt: native_evidence_model admit_coverage_result_v3 - the producer boundary - and therefore again at foundation close_run, which re-runs that exact admission over the RETAINED coverage payload. Refusals are native.coverage-cause-* and are PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION like the other producer-boundary refusals.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.selectedScalarCauseLimitation: STATED LIMITATION, not a defect to be engineered around. input-closure-incomplete retains ONE NativeCause while several missing inputs may coexist. Provenance of the selection: the producer names the cause it acted on, and Run closure checks that the named cause is lawful for the deficiency - it does not and cannot enumerate the inputs that were not named. What IS fully retained beside it is the rest of the Coverage entry and the Run's own evidence: the missing dependency sources, prepared rows and generated files are retained records in their own right, so a consumer that needs the complete set reads those rather than the scalar. No multi-cause format is introduced merely to make the prose true; the bounded source/ownership laws stay exactly as they are, and the limitation is published so no consumer reads the scalar as exhaustive.

x-opensip-public-route-registry.standing: Normative and CLOSED. The PUBLIC TERMINATION each internal decision key of the capability and Coverage-cause guards derives to. An earlier revision published prose placeholders here - `request detail ...`, `operational record` - as if they were public detail codes; 14 of 16 branch targets refused the real DomainDetail schema and none of the keys was in internalAliases. Prose is not an enum value, and the claim that those targets were already members was false. Every value below is either a member of the closed workflows common D9 vocabularies, a member of the closed public DomainDetailCode registry, or an explicit declaration that the optional DomainDetail is ABSENT with the real operational carrier named.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.carrier: The public carrier is workflows/schemas/common.schema.json#/$defs/StepTermination, not a bare DomainDetail. It carries `class` plus `errorCode`/`faultCause`/`reasonCodes`, and `domainDetail` is OPTIONAL. Where no existing DomainDetailCode member names the condition, domainDetail is lawfully ABSENT - the errorCode already names it - and the internal key is retained in the operational diagnostic record. That is the existing event law, not a new allowance.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.originatingBoundaryLaw: admission-and-qualification section 1 fixes the actor/layer split: `Invalid external input is an admission rejection with the existing carrier's D9 code; an invalid host-generated internal layer is a host invariant fault.` The inherited d9-exit-contract.v1.14 completes it: nonAnalysisDerivation rule 2 puts authored-config errors and failed preconditions in request-rejected, rule 5 puts HOST failures in operational-failed, and axes.domainCondition distinguishes `host-fault` from `precondition-failed`. So the same internal key derives a DIFFERENT class and code depending on where the bad value entered, and calling every retained or direct spec `host-generated` was wrong: a retained spec of known external origin is an external input, and only a host BUG minting its own invalid internal layer is a host fault.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.helperDoesNotGuessOrigin: The pure admission helpers - admit_requested_capabilities, admit_release_capability_registry, deficiency_cause_faults - are passed rows and nothing about provenance, so they emit the internal decision key ALONE. public_termination_for(key, origin) is the derivation the HOST calls with the origin it already holds; it refuses an origin the key cannot have, so a caller cannot launder a configuration error into a host fault or the reverse.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.hostInvariantSuccessor: SELECTED NORMATIVE D9 COMPOSITION, published here rather than deferred. It inherits docs/coop/artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json UNCHANGED and adds exactly one thing: the faultCause `host-invariant`, mapped to the EXISTING error code SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE. What was unrepresentable was the host-INVARIANT subtype specifically - other host-fault causes such as host-io, ledger-corrupt and provider-protocol already existed and were always representable - because StepTermination requires operational-failed to carry BOTH an errorCode and a non-none faultCause, and no declared cause named a host invariant violation. Borrowing host-io for it would be a different remedy. PRECISION: codeMaps.rule's `total and injective` is a property of the DECLARED CAUSE DOMAIN - every declared cause has exactly one code - and does NOT require every errorCode to have a preimage, so an errorCode without a cause was not a violation of totality; the earlier claim that the maps were non-total was wrong. Existing classes, exit codes, reason codes and error codes are unchanged, but this IS a D9 vocabulary extension: faultCause grows by one member, and saying otherwise would be false. Schema, workflow mapper and this registry must agree, every inherited mapping and golden is preserved, and an unknown cause still refuses.

x-opensip-public-route-registry.aliasMapIsContextFree: Only a key whose public DETAIL is the same for EVERY origin may appear in public-detail-registry internalAliases, because that map is context-free. Two keys qualify and are aliased there: native.requested-capability-mode-not-selected -> PROVIDER.NOT_SELECTED and native.release-capability-undeclared -> native.capability-unavailable. The origin-DEPENDENT keys deliberately are NOT in that map - a context-free alias cannot express `CONFIG.INVALID when configured, absent when the host produced it` - and the keys whose detail is absent need no alias because they never surface as a DomainDetailCode. An earlier revision claimed all 14 belonged there and that the edit was mechanical; both claims were wrong.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.enforcedAt: native_evidence_model public_termination_for derives the termination and validates it against the real StepTermination schema; the guards themselves emit only the internal key.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.possibleOriginsLaw: Every key declares the boundaries at which it CAN arise, and a derivation refuses any other. A release declaration is never a user's configuration and a configured capability is never the host's own authenticated release input, so a caller cannot launder one actor's fault into another's. An origin-INDEPENDENT key still has possible origins - what is independent is the resulting class and code, not who could have caused it.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.unsupportedTypedIsNotOnThisTable: An UNSUPPORTED-TYPED request is admitted and ANSWERED, never refused: the Run closes and its Coverage carries `unknown` with the deficiency the OWNING DERIVATION selects under the section 10 precedence. For a relation the admitted universe cannot serve at all - a compiler-free references request under syntax-only - that is language-tier-unsupported with capability-missing, and it OUTRANKS provider-unavailable. A capability the release merely did not declare available carries provider-unavailable with capability-missing only where no more specific deficiency applies, and a CANDIDATE-ONLY capability has no Coverage entry at all - its public route is the advisory native.capability-unavailable DomainDetail. An earlier revision stated the provider-unavailable pair here as THE outcome for both cases, which contradicted the precedence and the candidate-only distinction section 1.4 publishes. Neither case may be converted into an admission refusal.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.envelopeErrorsComposition: A kind=failure CommandEnvelope REQUIRES a nonempty `errors` array of DomainDetail, so `termination.domainDetail` being OPTIONAL does not complete the public failure surface: a route that lawfully leaves it absent still owes the envelope a detail. An earlier revision stopped at StepTermination admission, and a minimal failure envelope built from the externally-supplied and host-generated routes refused `errors is a required property`. failure_envelope_errors composes it: where the termination carries a detail the array is EXACTLY that detail, so the two surfaces can never disagree; where it does not, the route's own `envelopeDetail` supplies one. Every code used is a member of the closed public DomainDetailCode registry. Four members were ADDED there rather than borrowing an unrelated remedy - native.capability-spec-invalid, native.release-declaration-invalid, native.coverage-cause-unsupported and HOST.INVARIANT_VIOLATED - because `a supplied spec names an unregistered capability`, `the installed release declaration is malformed`, `the provider emitted an unsupported deficiency/cause pair` and `the host violated its own invariant` are four different things for a caller to do next. Reuse was taken wherever it was honest: external configuration keeps CONFIG.INVALID and a NOT-SELECTED cell keeps PROVIDER.NOT_SELECTED. Before a Plan or Run exists no run envelope is fabricated - the failure envelope carries the termination, its errors and the request id, and nothing else.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.subjectNormalization: The guards emit COLON-SUFFIXED refusal strings - native.requested-capability-unregistered:made-up-capability, native.coverage-cause-not-for-deficiency:input-closure-incomplete:capability-missing - so a normalizer matching the whole string would find no registered key. normalize_internal_key matches the LONGEST registered key followed by a colon and takes the remainder as the subject, which is what reaches DomainDetail.subject so a caller sees WHICH value was refused. A raw string matching no registered key REFUSES (native.public-route-key-unregistered) rather than passing through, as the public registry aliasRule requires of an unknown key; an origin a key cannot have refuses too (native.public-route-origin-not-possible).
x-opensip-public-route-registry.subjectBoundLaw: DomainDetail.subject is BoundedText (1024) while a refused VALUE can be far longer: a structurally valid languageMode may be 4096 characters, and the composed subject then reached 4149 and made the whole failure envelope schema-invalid at termination.domainDetail.subject or errors[0].subject. bounded_subject elides: the registered KEY is preserved verbatim - it selects the code, the class and the origin - and only the offending value is elided, keeping a leading window plus the SHA-256 of the untruncated subject's UTF-8 bytes. UNITS, because the two operations differ: `raw` is the composed subject as an admitted UNICODE SCALAR STRING, and length and slicing count UNICODE CODE POINTS - what BoundedText's JSON Schema maxLength counts - not UTF-8 bytes and not UTF-16 code units; the SHA-256 input is exactly raw encoded as UTF-8 with NO additional normalization, rendered as 64 lowercase hex characters after the ASCII marker `...#sha256:`, giving exactly 1024 code points. A non-ASCII value can therefore have a UTF-8 byte length above 1024 while its scalar length does not, and the two must not be conflated. GUARANTEE: distinct long values are distinguished under the ORDINARY COLLISION-RESISTANCE ASSUMPTION for SHA-256, not by any impossibility claim, and the guarantee is confined to what is PUBLISHED - the bounded subject and its digest. No separate retained store of the untruncated value is promised or named here; a host keeping its own operational log matches it by recomputing this digest. Emitting the untruncated string would be schema-invalid, dropping the subject would lose attribution, and reclassifying the input error as success would be false; the code, class and origin are never changed by the elision.

x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.standing: Normative and CLOSED. The per-language capability mapping of the bundled grammar set, published here so a consumer can reconstruct it without reading author code. syntaxClass is NOT caller-selected: a grammar row declaring a class other than the one this registry assigns to its languageId is refused at grammar-bundle admission, in both directions.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.source: native_evidence_model.v2.BUNDLED_GRAMMARS (the same table the shared discovery rule uses for the grammar-only membership path) and native-evidence section 6.3.

classLaw.code: The language has the section 6.3 body spans - function, method, closure/lambda, impl item and block bodies - and a published L2/L3 normalisation table. Bears clone body identity (clones@normalized-body-hash) and the code-construct syntax relations (declares/literal/control-flow @ syntactic). Its languageId MUST be a member of foundation body-language-version.languageId, because that identifier enters the clone preimage.
classLaw.data-document: A bundled grammar for a data or document format. It has no section 6.3 body spans, and this kit publishes no tokenisation, literalKind mapping or normalisation law for it. Its files are grammar-only MEMBERS - accounted, inventoried, never unsupported-file - bearing file/package/vcs-change inventory evidence under the syntax universe. It mints NO body identity, no suffix of it appears in the syntax dialect table, and its languageId MUST NOT be in body-language-version.languageId. A clone or code-construct request against it is explicitly UNAVAILABLE (language-tier-unsupported for that capability), never a complete empty clone result, which would read as a finding of no clones.

x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.unbundledLanguages: A language with no bundled grammar is not representable here at all: its files are unsupported-file with reason no-bundled-grammar, and its languageId is outside the SyntaxGrammarBundleV1 vocabulary. Adding one is a deliberate registry change, not a caller choice.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.futureCapability: Data-format syntax facts (for example literal@syntactic over JSON or YAML) would require a published tokenisation and literalKind law. None exists in this kit, so the mapping above does not promise them. This is a bounded future capability, deliberately not invented here.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.enforcementBoundaries: This registry is the authority at THREE boundaries, not one. (1) Grammar-bundle admission: a row's declared syntaxClass must equal the registered one, in both directions. (2) Every admitted fact2 under a syntax universe: every ANCHOR PATH must be read by a SELECTED grammar whose capability set contains that relation@rung. (3) Every requested subject-scope under a syntax universe, INCLUDING an empty view: judged on the committed examined extent, where a code capability needs at least one extent path read by a selected code grammar, and a capability no selected grammar bears is unavailable. INVENTORY CAPABILITIES (file@enumerated, package@manifest-declared, vcs-change@vcs-reported) are ALWAYS available and are never grammar-gated at boundary (2) OR boundary (3). An earlier revision stated that exemption only inside boundary (3), and boundary (2) read as an unconditional every-anchor rule; a literal implementer therefore refused the very inventory facts boundary (3) had just promised were unconditionally available, which made an inventoried .py path inventoriable and unrepresentable at the same time. The exemption belongs to both because it is a property of the RELATION, not of the boundary: an inventory fact is not read by a grammar at all - it is the snapshot inventory row, the manifest declaration or the VCS observation - so there is no grammar for it to be gated on. Independently of this exemption the relation registry anchorLaw closes the inventory class at ZERO anchors, so an inventory fact names no anchor path for boundary (2) to test in the first place; the two laws agree and neither depends on the other. An earlier revision enforced only (1), which constrains what a bundle says about itself and not what a Run claims: Markdown declares facts, complete empty declares/clones Coverage and references@resolved-binding under resolutionAttempted=false all admitted. None of the three consults a claimed coverage value, a caller-declared class, or whether facts exist.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.unavailableRequestDisclosure: A well-formed request for a capability this universe cannot serve is DISCLOSED, not answered and not refused outright: coverage `unknown`, deficiency `language-tier-unsupported`, nativeCause `capability-missing` - existing vocabulary, mapped in native-evidence section 10. A false `complete`, a wrong or null cause and a wrong deficiency each refuse with their own typed reason. The capability is retained: a data-grammar inventory Run and a code-grammar declares/clones Run still close with a genuine complete and no deficiency.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.selectionMatters: An UNSELECTED grammar lends no capability. Selection is committed in the universe identity, so a bundle that ships a grammar the universe did not select cannot make its capabilities available.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.inventoryIsNotGrammarGated: Normative. A snapshot inventories every file it contains, including ones no bundled grammar reads, so requiring a grammar per inventory row would silently narrow the promise this registry makes. The three inventory capabilities are therefore exempt at every boundary this registry owns, on every path - unsupported suffix, extensionless, data-document and code alike - and a `vcs-change` on a `deleted` path that is not in the snapshot at all. This is an exemption from GRAMMAR OWNERSHIP only. It does not exempt an inventory fact from its relation's snapshot joins (path in the inventory; for `file` also the content digest, the byte length and custody of the retained bytes), from own-scope attribution, or from the anchorLaw; and it does not make a CODE fact admissible merely because some other anchor of the same Run is on a supported path.

NativeCause.description: The typed cause carried beside a DeficiencyV2 in a Coverage entry. The three body-language-* members are the clones ownership states that identity-and-evidence and native-evidence section 11 require the clones Coverage to DISCLOSE: the contract mandates that such a scope mint no body identity, that its Coverage report the incompleteness, and that the predicate and seal be indeterminate rather than a false pass -- and until these members existed no value in this closed vocabulary could name why. A nullable nativeCause does not satisfy a mandated disclosure; a null there records that a disclosure was owed and not made. The other selectionLaw causes deliberately have NO member here: BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_COMPILED and BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_SELECTED are per-body refusals that section 11 states are compatible with coverage=complete (the host examined that subject and correctly produced no fact for it), and BODY_LANGUAGE_DIALECT_ABSENT/BODY_LANGUAGE_DIALECT_AMBIGUOUS are universe-level dialect faults that refuse before any Coverage entry is minted.

capabilityId.description: A member of native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json#/capabilities[].id. The pattern is the product-configuration analysis.capabilities item pattern, which contains no `@`, so a relation@rung spelling is refused by shape before membership is even consulted. Membership itself is checked at admission: the pattern is necessary and never sufficient.

languageModes.description: The language modes this release declares the capability applicable to. Each must be a registered mode whose (capability, mode) cell is not NOT-SELECTED.

ReleaseCapabilityDeclarationV1.description: One row of the authenticated release declaration registry named by native-evidence section 1.4 and admission-and-qualification section 1.1. SyntaxGrammarBundleV1.description: The installed, closure-bound grammar bundle that a syntax-only analysis parses with. It is the component that INTERPRETS a body span in that mode, so it is pinned exactly the way a toolchain is: closureId names an admitted kind=grammar closure, parserVersion must equal that closure manifest's semanticVersion (admission refuses native.syntax-grammar-version-not-from-manifest otherwise, mirroring the compiler-version rule), and bundleDigest is the exact retained bundle identity. `grammars` is the CLOSED bundled-grammar set: it is what native-evidence section 1.2's 'any file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar' actually denotes, and what makes `unsupported-file / no-bundled-grammar` decidable rather than a matter of taste.

parserName.description: The component that reads the body span. Not a compiler: a syntax-only universe executes none, and naming one here would claim an interpretation that never happened.

languageId.description: Every language the host actually bundles a grammar for, matching BUNDLED_GRAMMARS exactly. An earlier revision listed only typescript/javascript/rust and claimed equality with the body-language-version enum as a drift check; that could not express the four data/document grammars the host has always bundled, so native-evidence section 1.2's 'any file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar' was unrepresentable for them. What is actually held equal to the body-language-version enum is the set of languages whose grammars are syntaxClass=code - see syntaxClass.

syntaxClass.description: Which capability this grammar's files bear, and the exact distinction the original contracts already draw. `code`: the language has the body spans native-evidence section 6.3 defines - function, method, closure/lambda, impl item and block bodies - and a published L1-L3 normalisation table, so its files can bear clone body identity and the code-construct syntax relations. Its languageId MUST be a member of the foundation body-language-version languageId enum, because that identifier goes into the clone preimage. `data-document`: a bundled grammar for a data or document format with no such body spans and no published tokenisation, literalKind mapping or normalisation law anywhere in this kit. Its files are grammar-only members - accounted, never `unsupported-file` - and bear inventory evidence (file/package/vcs-change); they mint no body identity, and its languageId MUST NOT be in the body-language-version enum, since it can never appear in a clone preimage. Claiming code-construct syntax facts for a data format would require a tokenisation law this kit does not publish, which is exactly the fabricated-semantics failure the syntax-only universe exists to avoid.

normalizer.description: The clone normalisation component this bundle ships. SyntaxNativeContextV2.description: The native context of the syntax-only language mode. It carries exactly the grammar bundle that interprets a body span and nothing else: no toolchain, no stdlib, no lockfile, no node_modules layout, no config graph. Those all belong to resolution, and a grammar-only analysis performs none. A syntax-only context that named a compiler would be asserting semantics the mode never computes.

SyntaxUniverseV2ResolvedInputs.description: The universe of the syntax-only mode. Its identity is the admitted grammar context plus the SELECTED grammar set for this analysis: selecting a different grammar set is a different universe, exactly as selecting different compilation targets is for Rust, so what was parsed is visible to every consumer rather than being an invisible default. It carries the constant resolutionAttempted=false so no consumer can read a syntax-only universe as a resolution claim: semantic rungs under it are language-tier-unsupported, not merely absent.

selectedGrammarIds.description: A subset of the context bundle's grammarIds. Admission refuses a selection naming a grammar the bundle does not contain; an empty selection is not expressible, because a universe that parsed nothing could not have produced a fact.

configProjectionSha256.description: The 64-hex suffix of H(native.cargo-config-projection.v2, CargoConfigProjectionV2) over the bound context configProjection record. A bare DigestHex, never a Sha256Text, and never the raw SHA-256 of the canonical projection bytes.

sourceUnitOwnershipId.description: Required and nullable, exactly as preparedOutputSetId is. null means NO committed ownership: such a universe admits no clones fact AT ALL, whatever its edition map looks like. An earlier revision of this description said null was admissible 'only while the edition map has a single distinct value, where every body has the same dialect and no owner selection arises'. That was the withdrawn package-default fast path and it is contradicted by the retained selectionLaw and by body_language_version, which refuses on missing ownership unconditionally: Cargo lets a target override its package default, so even a single-valued edition map can contain targets at different effective editions, and agreeing package defaults therefore never determine a body's dialect. The nullable form is retained deliberately - a universe whose ownership is unavailable or only partially enumerated is a legitimate retained universe; it simply mints no body identity, its clones Coverage carries the typed ownership disclosure (deficiency input-closure-incomplete with the matching body-language-* nativeCause), and its empty clone view stays indeterminate rather than becoming a finding of no clones.

TypeScriptNativeContextV2.description: Closed native context for the typescript-v2 universe; H domain `native.context.typescript.v2`. It carries no platform FIELD because TypeScript resolution semantics are platform-invariant by design (section 1.1); the identity is NOT platform-invariant, because toolClosure.closureId names a signed closure whose foundation descriptor includes `platform`, so two platform families running different executables mint two nativeContextIds. It is NOT NativeContextV2, which is the Rust context (targetTriple/hostTriple/cargo resolver); a typescript-v2 universe whose nativeContextId was minted from a Rust descriptor is refused.

It is a native-context selector, not a source language; the LANGUAGE of a body under it is still one of the closed body-language-version languageId values.

CoverageAdmissionV1.description: Result of the admitted native producer boundary for one CoverageResultV3 payload: the host mints scope2 from its own subject enumeration and refuses a payload whose committed key disagrees. A provider-supplied commitment is never authority.

ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1.description: The retained resolution read-set layout a TypeScript context commits to when nodeModulesInReadSet is true. One row per installed package DIRECTORY the resolver may read: installPath is the project-relative directory as the resolver walks it, realPath is the project-relative directory after symlink/workspace-link resolution (equal to installPath when there is no link), and contentSha256 is the raw SHA-256 of that package directory manifest file bytes (its package.json) as RETAINED, joined by digest. These rows are deliberately NOT snapshot inventory rows and must not be read as any: the one shared discovery rule prunes node_modules by path segment, so an inventory row could not exist for them, and the layout is a retained resolution observation of bytes the analysis actually read (native-evidence section 2.2, and the blobJoin -- not a snapshotJoin -- on the native.context.typescript.v2 nested record). The earlier wording said 'as inventoried in the snapshot', which contradicted both and would have led an implementer to add node_modules paths to the snapshot inventory. Rows are strictly ascending and unique by installPath, so one layout has one spelling. nodeModulesLayoutDigest is the raw SHA-256 of C(this record); it is null exactly when nodeModulesInReadSet is false.

extendsResolved.description: The ORDERED resolved extends edges of this node, in the order the config declares them. TypeScript 5.0 supports multiple entries in `extends` and a LATER entry wins, so precedence is the array order and must be retained: an unordered set or a single edge cannot represent an ordinary modern configuration. Empty means this node extends nothing. Repeated edges are retained; this is a sequence, not a set.

TypeScriptConfigGraphV1.description: The resolved tsconfig/jsconfig extends graph a TypeScript universe commits to. entryConfigPath is the SELECTED root config the program was opened with, null exactly when the configuration was synthesized; nodes is every config file actually read, strictly ascending and unique by path, each carrying its inventoried snapshot digest, its kind and its ORDERED resolved extends edges with later-wins precedence. configOrigin is derived from the ENTRY node kind, never from the whole set: a jsconfig.json that extends a shared base.json is a jsconfig program. Every node must be reachable from the entry, every edge must name another node, and the edge graph must be acyclic. tsconfigGraphHash is the raw SHA-256 of C(this record). A selected entry whose kind is other represents an explicitly selected custom-named TypeScript configuration and derives configOrigin tsconfig.

SourceUnitOwnershipV1.description: The committed relation from a SNAPSHOT SOURCE PATH to the compilation TARGET that reads it, the closed table of those targets, and the EXPLICIT SELECTION of which of them this universe analyses. It exists because a body span dialect is a property of the compilation target: neither a crate-name-to-root map nor the package edition map can supply it, since #[path], files shared by several targets and several compilation contexts of one crate defeat a directory inference, and Cargo lets a target override its package default edition. Because this record is committed by H identity inside RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs.sourceUnitOwnershipId, a different SELECTION is a different record, a different identity and therefore a DIFFERENT sourceUniverse: one physical source path compiled by two targets at two editions is validly analysed under each, one selection at a time, with no change to any relation payload. Every row is a retained native observation; nothing here executes Cargo, a build script or a repository read, and nothing here qualifies a compiler or an enumerator.

enumeration.description: complete: every compiled source path OF THE SELECTED UNITS has a row, so a path with no row is not compiled by any selected target. partial: the producer did not finish, so an owner INSIDE the selected scope may exist that is not listed. These are different claims and the second is not a weaker form of the first: an unlisted owner could contradict a listed one, so no clone body dialect is admissible under partial. That is checked BEFORE any row lookup, so partial discovery can never act as an implicit edition selection by hiding a conflicting owner. Partial evidence remains useful under the existing facts and Coverage law: the clones scope reports its incompleteness and the predicate is indeterminate, rather than a body identity being minted on an unbounded claim.

units.description: The closed table of compilation targets. Strictly unique by unitId, and unitId is a FUNCTION of the metadata, so two contradictory rows for one purported unit are a refusal rather than two units that differ by accident. A selection or an ownership row naming a unitId with no row here is an unbound caller label and is inadmissible.

unitId.description: H(native.compilation-unit.v1, UnitIdentityV1{schemaVersion:1, markerPath, targetKind, targetName}) over the very fields this row carries. DERIVED retention: nothing separate is retained because the preimage IS the row, and admission re-derives and compares (sourceUnitOwnership.unitId). Not an opaque digest - preimage record, domain and selector are all published - and not a delimiter label, which could stay injective only by narrowing admitted repository paths.

markerPath.description: The inventoried manifest that declares this target: the same markerPath vocabulary WorkspaceUnitV2 already uses, cited rather than duplicated. WorkspaceUnitV2 and UnitMembershipV1 identify WORKSPACE units - cargo-package and cargo-workspace - which is the wrong granularity here, because one package holds several targets that may carry different editions; naming the marker joins the two rather than competing with them.

crateName.description: A key of the universe edition map, which supplies the package default.

targetEdition.description: The target's OWN edition when it sets one, null when it takes the package default. Cargo documents edition on a target as well as on a package: cargo-metadata lists targets[].edition and states the package edition is a DEFAULT individual targets may differ from. null DEFERS to the universe edition map for crateName, so the two committed places can never contradict: an override is explicit and visible, and its absence is explicit too.

selectedUnitIds.description: The EXPLICIT analysis scope: the compilation targets this universe analyses. Every member must be a unitId of the units table. This is what makes a shared path representable at two editions without an ambiguous claim - two selections are two universes - and it is what distinguishes SELECTED SCOPE from INCOMPLETE ENUMERATION. An owner outside the selection is deliberately out of scope and its edition does not bear on a body; an unlisted owner INSIDE the selection is a gap in knowledge and refuses. Silently omitting a conflicting owner from the units table is not a selection: the omission is invisible, whereas a selection is committed in the identity.

ownership.description: The pure relation. It carries no edition and no metadata, so it cannot contradict the units table.

UnitIdentityV1.description: The closed PREIMAGE of a compilation unit identity, published here with its domain, codec and selector precisely so that unitId is not an opaque digest: any consumer can rebuild these four fields from the unit row that carries them and recompute the identity. A delimiter-joined label was the earlier draft and is WITHDRAWN - it was injective only by excluding # from markerPath, and a # in a repository directory is admissible under the canonical repository-path contract, so that recipe narrowed admitted paths to make a delimiter work. H over this projection needs no such restriction and is fixed width for every admitted path and name length.

x-opensip-digest-law.standing: The closing digest law of identity-and-evidence section 3, extended to this bundle. Every 64-hex or sha256: field here carries x-opensip-digest naming its representation, retention and authority. There is no default and no residue: a new field added without an annotation is inadmissible, exactly as in identity-schemas.v2.

retention.preimage: the exact preimage bytes are retained under this digest
retention.preimage-frame: the retained object is the H preimage frame, so SHA256(retained bytes) is the digest
retention.closure-tree-member: the digest must be a member digest of the retained signed closure tree the annotation names
retention.owner-retained: the named owning contract retains and admits the bytes; this bundle joins by digest equality
